💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chinese automakers are trying to capture as much of the European car market as possible, and they’re resorting to clever marketing tricks that legacy automakers have used in the past to attract buyers.
  • Sources indicate that BYD is one of the many Chinese car companies trying to rack up orders, and its Denza brand has now recreated a famous Volkswagen commercial from two decades ago that involved a diesel-powered SUV and a jumbo jet.
  • I vividly remember when I saw the original clip 20 years ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chinese automakers are trying to capture as much of the European car market as possible, and they’re resorting to clever marketing tricks that legacy automakers have used in the past to attract buyers.

Sources indicate that BYD is one of the many Chinese car companies trying to rack up orders, and its Denza brand has now recreated a famous Volkswagen commercial from two decades ago that involved a diesel-powered SUV and a jumbo jet. Only this time, Denza has an ace up its sleeve, and it’s quite impressive.

I vividly remember when I saw the original clip 20 years ago. A blue Volkswagen Touareg V10 diesel towed a 171-ton jet aircraft down the same Dunsfold runway in the United Kingdom where the old "Top Gear" episodes used to be filmed.

Now, the Denza B5 (or Bao 5 in some markets) plug-in hybrid SUV is back at the same place to do the same stunt, but adapted for a 2026 where everything seemingly needs to be bigger, more over the top, and more in-your-face. (I blame TikTok.).

So, we have a Chinese PHEV that uses two electric motors and a 1.5-liter gas engine. It’s all-wheel-drive, its 31.8-kilowatt-hour battery can deliver up to 56 miles of all-electric range on a full battery, and it has two mechanical locking differentials. This last part is notable. The battery can be fast-charged at up to 100 kW, and the total system output is a healthy 536 horsepower, with most of that oomph being provided by the two e-motors.

We also have a 207-ton jumbo jet that got a quick repositioning for no other purpose than pure entertainment.

Here comes the interesting bit: While Volkswagen’s original stunt kept all four of the Touareg’s wheels in place—you know, how a car usually works—BYD decided to put its PHEV SUV to the test by gradually removing some wheels.

Industry observers note that the first run was done with all four wheels in place, followed by a three-wheeled run with 2.2 tons of ballast. For the final act, both right wheels were removed, and the ballast reached 5 tonnes. During the three runs, the Denza B5 towed the Boeing 747-400 over one mile, and best of all, it used exclusively electric power.

The point of it all? Promote the newly introduced SUV to the UK market, where the Land Rover Defender is among its biggest rivals. Unlike the Defender, however, which is now based on a unibody design and is primarily combustion-powered, the Denza B5 sits on a bespoke ladder-frame chassis and more substantially electrified. It has a gas engine that acts mainly as a generator for the high-voltage battery. The battery cells are directly integrated between the chassis rails.

Sources indicate that if you're thinking about trying this stunt at home, just know the vehicle needed a few modifications to pull it off. BYD added a custom towing attachment, removed some seats to make room for the ballast, and added stabilizers to make up for the missing wheels.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside of China for the first time ever – and its starting its push for global growth with the UAE in 2027.
  • Xiaomi is selling its electrified vehicles to buyers outside of China for first time this week, with the SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV now listed for sale throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside of China for the first time ever – and its starting its push for global growth with the UAE in 2027.

Xiaomi is selling its electrified vehicles to buyers outside of China for first time this week, with the SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV now listed for sale throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The firm isn’t going it alone, however.

Xiomi is working local distributor Gargash Prime Automotive, rather than operating its own retail network, with Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun confirming that the organization would officially enter Western car markets next year at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen held 17NOV.

CarNewsChina reports that Gargash Prime Automotive is offering 13 variants across the Xiaomi SU7 sedan, YU7 SUV, and Skynomad extended-range electric SUV lineup, with retail prices starting at 169,900 AED ($~46,200 US) for the SU7 Standard and climbing all the way up to 375,900 AED ($~102,000 US) for the range-topping SU7 Ultra.

Not to lump a bunch of nations with their own rich heritage and car culture together, but it’s fair to say that drivers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait love their supercars – and the brand’s Xiaomi SU7 Ultra might be one of the most super of them all, thanks to fully 1,548 hp from three high-torque electric motors, the SU7 Ultra can sprint from 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in under two seconds on its way to a towering, 217 mph top speed.

It’s not just a straight-line speed machine, either. Xiaomi gave its go-fast flagship a serious track-focused makeover on its way to becomig the “Utlra,” complete with carbon-ceramic brakes, an aggressive (if controversial) composite aero package, an enormous rear wing, and a chassis tuned to tackle the turns the Green Hell of the Nürburgring.

And, at a relatively reasonable $102,000 equivalent price, I’d be willing to bet that a lot of the hypercar-loving Emiratis will be eager to get their hands on one.

The first customer deliveries of the Xiaomi SU7 Standard and Ultra, YU7 Standard, and Skynomad N70 Pro models are scheduled for December of this year, with deliveries of the remaining variants scheduled for February 2027.

Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

📅 23 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (459 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died.
  • According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles.
  • Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

It has been revealed that zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

According to recent reports, zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Did Max Verstappen like the Las Vegas Grand Prix that he dominated on Saturday night, as a racer? No.

The four-time champion under the former regulations continues to be outspoken about his judgment of F1’s current ‘nimble’ car regulations, which put more weight on battery management in the 50/50 hybrid system than on racing itself.

From the cockpit, Verstappen took the lead into the opening corner and managed his race from there.

When asked if he remembered the last time he won a race with the field so close, with so much jockeying for position, Verstappen almost caught himself before delivering the headline for this article and countless more.

“I probably shouldn’t say it; I probably should not,” Verstappen started in the press conference. “I remember winning one like this when I was playing on Mario Kart.

“Sometimes, you drop back, and you get drafted, and there’s catch-up, always; when you drop back, you go faster.

“That’s the last time I felt something like this, Verstappen finished.

What was, from the outside, a thrilling race, where the field was able to play cat-and-mouse with Verstappen, make up ground, and pass, was for the leader not even enough to raise his heart rate.

In a recent development, this was Verstappen’s fourth win in six races after a slow start for Red Bull and their upcoming Ford Power Units. A change of tides to be proud of, even in a race that didn’t spark joy for the racer.

“When I look at it from my racer heart, no,” Verstappen answered when asked if he enjoyed the ‘crazy racing’ of the GP.

Sources indicate that “When you look at it as a show, a spectacle, yes. I’ve enjoyed my repasting and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart, and no.

Even my heart rate- I was not nervous at all. It felt kinda cruising out there. Just try to press the battery whenever it was passing or to defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, you probably like it.

Verstappen has elected not to take part in the new Whoop F1 partnership that would show fans a driver's heart rate throughout the race.

Lando Norris, who finished second after spending the first half of the race outside the points, felt similar to Verstappen about the focus of the race, saying he paid more attention to energy deployment than what was actually in front of him.

In a recent development, “The whole race was judging the battery the whole time,” Norris mentioned. “I was looking at the battery more than I’m looking where I’m going around this track.”.

In a recent development, the last time Hyundai unveiled a fresh work truck was 22 years ago, and the Hyundai Porter has proven itself as a dependable workhorse throughout Korea and Southeast Asia – but only the pyramids and the Chevy Express can last forever. Hyundai is reportedly getting ready to pull the wraps off an all-new Porter pickup. This time, it’s electric.

Distinct from the Piaggio-branded Porter pickup that’s already sold in Europe, the Hyundai Porter is a conceptually similar, work-focused vehicle with a dropside pickup “bed” trailing a box-like passenger cab and a serious, professional-grade payload capacity.

Carscoops recently published photos of a heavily camouflaged Hyundai Porter prototype last month, along with claims that Hyundai means to follow up the success of sister brand Kia’s multifunctional PV5 electric vans with a globally available electric version of the truck as early as next year. This week, the wraps came off, giving us our best look yet at what the truck might look like when it makes its official debut.

Sources indicate that after feeding as many spy shots as I could into some AI models, we ended up with the images you see here. If they’re accurate, they show a commercial-ready EV that’s meant to attract newly introduced fleet buyers looking to ditch diesel in Western markets while serving as a direct, 1:1 replacement for domestic fleet operators already putting Porter pickups to work.

Those operators will probably feel a little safer behind the wheel of the newly introduced truck, too. Hyundai has worked a short hood and crash structure into the bodywork where a conventional “flat” cabover now sits – a move that seems to point both to a commitment to provide better front-end protection to the truck’s occupants and an intent to at least take an honest run at the Euro NCAP crash standards.

In a recent development, beyond that, we don’t really know anything about the upcoming Korean pickup – but it’s a safe bet that the next-generation Porter will benefit from some of the technology that’s been baked into the Hyundai Motor Group’s E-GMP.S commercial vehicle platform that underpins the Kia PV vehicles. Those ship with 51.5 and 71.2 kWh battery options sending electrons to 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motors, and while that’s far from a guarantee, it’s not nothing, either.

It has been revealed that that’s my take, anyway – what’s yours? Will the Hyundai Porter EV make its way to the West on an AWD version of the E-GMP.S platform, or will it remain a regional model running on one of the company’s hybrid platforms? Let us know in the comments.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (585 w)

Industry News: This EV-Swapped 1967 Porsche 912 Has 300 HP And A Split Battery Pack

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Inverted is a name that's been around for a while in the EV-swap world.
  • According to Piston Heads, the owner of this specific 912 had already swapped a more potent 911 engine into its rear end, but wanted something even better suited for daily driving.
  • Industry observers note that there's some clever engineering here, too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Inverted is a name that's been around for a while in the EV-swap world. It started out doing electric powertrain swaps for classic Range Rovers, which it still does. But it also has a bespoke program now, under which it will develop custom EV swaps for customers for any sort of car they want. In this specific case, Inverted stuffed some batteries and an electric motor into an old Porsche 912. Interestingly, this is the third powertrain that's been in this Porsche.

According to Piston Heads, the owner of this specific 912 had already swapped a more potent 911 engine into its rear end, but wanted something even better suited for daily driving. So they took their car to Inverted and the team got to work. The end result is a car that looks exactly like a normal Porsche 912, with all of its gorgeous old-school styling, but drives like a modern EV.

Industry observers note that there's some clever engineering here, too. The 62 kWh battery pack is more than enough to propel the vintage Porsche's featherweight body a fair ways. However, that's a lot of weight to hang over the rear axle. Air-cooled Porsches were already prone to lift-off oversteer, so they don't need any more. So Inverted came up with an interesting solution: split the pack into two parts. On section is mounted out back where the engine used to be, and the other is under the hood. It means the electric 912's weight balance is actually better than the original car's.

Recent findings suggest that inverted claims that this EV 912 has around 250 miles of range, and it can DC fast charge at 75 kW. The latter might seem weak in the world of modern EVs, but it's perfectly fine in a classic like this. This is a daily driver, not a long-distance cruiser. So 250 miles is more than enough for daily usage, and plugging it in overnight to charge will get the owner a fresh battery in the morning.

The rear-mounted electric motor makes 300 horsepower, so it's much more potent than the original 912 four-cylinder engine which made around 90 horsepower. Inverted notes it can hit 0-60 mph in four seconds, which kicks the ass of the stock vehicle. The original 912 took about 13 seconds.

This isn't just a powertrain swap, either. Its interior is completely redone and it's gorgeous. The gauges look like vintage Porsche gauges but they're modified for EV used. For example, the classic Porsche central tachometer was replaced with a power percentage gauge. The fuel gauge is now an analog battery charge gauge, too. It's just lovely.

This is an awesome project and one that would make for an incredible daily driver. It has modern Porsche levels of performance, with modern EV levels of range, in a stylish vintage package. Seems perfect.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The enhancement is also adding some key latest features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and latest Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

The Australian surfer-turned-DJ FISHER took an early lead and controlled the pace of the LEGO race, much like his Red Bull Racing counterpart did in the weekend’s Grand Prix.

Eleven stars represented one of the current F1 teams on the grid in their own Lego minicars.

FISHER was one of the 11 celebrities tasked with piloting a fully functional Lego minicar around the FIA-rated street circuit of Las Vegas, along with the likes of actors Hannah Waddingham, Brendan Hunt, Caleb McLaughlin, Jack Whitehall and Terry Crews, singer LISA, gold-medal gymnast Jordon Chiles, chef Gordon Ramsay, a Magician named Dynamo and fellow DJ Carl Cox.

FISHER, a Red Bull-sponsored DJ, represented the brand and arrived fully decked out in a Red Bull firesuit, trying to stand above the competition.

Michelin Star-holding Ramsay was the first celebrity to be caught chatting, reaching out to grab LISA’s Ferrari-sponsored Lego minicar in hopes of regaining his position.

In the end, FISHER shared the podium with Chiles and Waddingham as the trio collected their comically oversized Lego trophies in gold, silver, and bronze.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that developed by Japanese material handling giant Tadano, the 35-ton V320RC wheeled electric pick & carry crane has spent the last few months proving itself at NMG Italia’s job sites, where it’s been handling heavy loads in tight industrial spaces and improving efficiency by 50%. And now, you can buy one.

Developed in collaboration with NMG Italia, the V320RC electric crane has already proven its performance in the field with NMG and during precision setup operations at Marmomac, a trade show dedicated to the marble industry held each year in Verona.

Sources indicate that “The (Tadano) V320RC marks a real breakthrough in the pick & carry industry,” reads the official Tadano launch copy. “Rather than an evolution of existing solutions, it introduces a upcoming philosophy, with technologies and features capable of setting new benchmarks in the lifting market. Tadano and NMG Italia continue their collaboration in the field, turning real-world experience into new technological solutions to meet the most advanced demands of industrial lifting.”.

The crane itself is a compact, battery-electric pick-and-carry machine with a maximum lifting capacity of 35 tonnes. Measuring just 5 m long, 2.15 m wide and 2.400 m tall (a meter is about a yard, guys – you got this), the V320RC is designed to bring heavy lifting capability into tight industrial spaces where larger cranes struggle to operate.

It has been revealed that the upcoming Tadano runs on a 120V, 1,120 Ah li-ion battery pack (that works out to ~134 kWh) and packs a gross vehicle weight of more than 31,150 kg (~34.5 short tones). That number includes 9,500 kg (~10 tons) of removable counterweights that make transport and handling easier for a wider range of customers. Under the hood, a new hydraulic system pairs a variable-displacement pump with what the firm calls “an electro-hydraulic control valve” to improve precision and responsiveness while reducing energy consumption.

According to NMG Italia, all that baked-in tech V320RC give them 50% better productivity than competing electric cranes working under equivalent workloads, with enough battery capacity to support several days of operation between charges.

Waymo Is Recalling Its Robotaxis Because They're Not Great At Dealing With Human Instructions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo recalled its robotaxis again on Friday, citing issues with navigating closed freeway lanes and handling manually controlled intersections.
  • The company's robotaxis were banned from California freeways earlier this month after a few high-profile incidents.
  • The robotaxis seem to be very adept at dealing with normal road conditions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo recalled its robotaxis again on Friday, citing issues with navigating closed freeway lanes and handling manually controlled intersections. For anyone who has been following Waymo closely, this shouldn't be that surprising.

The company's robotaxis were banned from California freeways earlier this month after a few high-profile incidents. Waymo took the voluntary step of suspending interstate operation nationwide on Wednesday, meaning the entire fleet is now back to running primarily on local roads and minor state highways.

The robotaxis seem to be very adept at dealing with normal road conditions. But the trouble seems to be when something unexpected pops up. Regulators from California cited poor behavior surrounding closed lanes and construction zones, a recurring issue for the manufacturer, along with a another recent high-profile incident involving a California Highway Patrol rolling road block.

Industry observers note that if you don't know what that last sentence means, you aren't alone. When I first moved to California a few years ago, I had no idea what a rolling road block or "traffic break" meant in normal parlance. But drive California freeways long enough and you'll experience one. A CHP cruiser or a group of them joins the highway, puts on its lights, and slowly zigzags across all lanes of traffic, blocking drivers from passing or exceeding the speed of the maneuver. The goal is typically to create a safe break in traffic for authorities to removed debris, clear and accident, or otherwise operate on the road. Sometimes it just slows down the herd before it barrels into a blind-corner accident scene at 80 mph.

Sources indicate that when I first experienced this, I was plenty confused. But when I saw cops swerving in front of me with lights on, I naturally just slowed down and stayed behind me. Common sense told me that a cop swerving around with their lights on probably isn't looking for a race. Unfortunately, though, autonomous driving software doesn't always know how to interpret novel situations. So when a Waymo got caught behind a rolling road block, here's what it did:.

It has been revealed that yep, it tried to blow right by. CHP was able to hold it back, but I've seen a Trooper controlling six lanes of traffic with one car before. Add in an inventive and disobedient robotaxi and you can see how it could create a dangerous situation wherein an autonomous vehicle is driving down a road that construction workers or police think is effectively closed.

According to recent reports, now, Waymos are good enough at avoiding hitting things that I don't expect this would have been too bad. But even a small chance of a runaway robotaxi is unacceptable to regulators and to Waymo, so it's good to pause freeway operations until they figure things out.

It has been revealed that but the road block situation is indicative of a larger problem with autonomous vehicles, and perhaps the most interesting one. We think of driving as a predominantly legal or process-driven endeavor. You stop at stop signs, obey the speed limit, and keep it between the lines. Errors happen, but we tend to see them as based on improperly applied rules.

Industry observers note that yet the police here are disrupting the rules and enforcing an unscheduled and ad-hoc temporary speed limit and traffic flow. If you're from out of state or haven't experienced it yet, it's confusing, as there's direct ruleset for an impromptu situation like that. Yet any other driver caught in this situation wouldn't blow past the cop car. Like me, they'd approach it cautiously, and let the police car take the lead.

In a recent development, that is the issue I'm referring to: Driving is not just about rules and infrastructure. It's a social behavior. We wave each other ahead at stop signs and intersections. We signal our intent for an aggressive merge by riding the side of the lane market. You look at people's faces to gaze intention and attention. And when the traffic lights are down or the road is blocked by falling trees, we create impromptu order where chaos exists, nodding or waving to signal that it's someone else's term.

This was always going to be the hard part for robotaxis. That's why the same recall applies to another troubled behavioral pattern for Waymos: They struggle when officers or city workers are manually controlling and intersection. Whether it's due to a high-traffic event or an outage, it's not all that uncommon to see a police officer directing traffic by hand. They wave you through or hold you back.

Industry observers note that but what happens if the car loses sight of the person directing traffic? What if the person directing traffic isn't actually a police officer, and waves you through a red light? What if the alternate route the police point you to spits the robotaxi onto a highway, where it isn't allowed to go?

There are a million more what-ifs related to this social component of driving. All of them will have to be encountered and solved as they come, just as you and I eventually figured these things out. Recall by recall, we'll turn these Waymos into upstanding citizens.

  • According to recent reports, since our last patch around the 10,000-mile mark, the Palisade has seen shorter trips to Elk Rapids and Traverse City in Michigan, as well as to Cedar Point in Ohio, but it’s also made it as far as Colorado and West Virginia.
  • See all results for upcoming 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 28262.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that everyone at Car and Driver loves a road trip, and it’s clear that our editors play favorites when choosing a long-term car for said road trips. Often when traveling, an editor is rolling deep with family, friends, pets, and gear, so one of our more spacious vehicles usually ends up going along for the ride. With a few large cars at our disposal, the team has options, but after 20,000 miles, it’s clear that our long-term Hyundai Palisade Hybrid tends to be the first choice.

According to recent reports, since our last patch around the 10,000-mile mark, the Palisade has seen shorter trips to Elk Rapids and Traverse City in Michigan, as well as to Cedar Point in Ohio, but it’s also made it as far as Colorado and West Virginia. Deputy video editor Carlos Lago loaded the Hyundai with his family, their dog, a travel crib, a dog bed, and luggage, and the Palisade Hybrid handled it all without issue. In the logbook, Lago noted that the Palisade was “smooth, decently powerful, and adept at maintaining the higher freeway speeds up north, though the road and tire noise was louder than I’d like at those speeds.”.

See all results for upcoming 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 28262.

According to recent reports, entry and exit haven’t proved as smooth as the Palisade’s ride, though. Lago—and other editors, including yours truly—bemoaned the hands-free door access, which will occasionally lock the doors instead of unlocking them. At that point, we just pull out the key fob, eliminating the point of that tech entirely.

Recent findings suggest that the Palisade Hybrid’s largely white interior is another point of contention for staffers with kids, friends, and pets that ride in the back seat. Those of us with young children in car seats, particularly rear-facing ones, cringe at the footprints and mess we know is coming. Senior features editor Greg Fink hopped in at around 15,000 miles and wondered, “Is it just me, or is this interior looking a little worse for the wear?” With 20,000 miles still to go, we’re hoping that wear stays within reason.

Testing director Dave VanderWerp thought the Palisade Hybrid was a fantastic family SUV with a lot of features not available in other competitive SUVs, but he was still frustrated by parts of the road-trip experience. He found the cargo hold lacking capacity with the third row in use, though his teenagers did manage to occupy that row comfortably. Folding and unfolding the second row proved tricky for VanderWerp’s passengers. A recall on those seats may have added some difficulty there.

Technical editor Austin Irwin had high praise for the Palisade’s interior: “You can just about close your eyes and imagine you’re driving a Genesis.” That being mentioned, he wasn’t blown away by the hybrid powertrain on the highway, where it was flipping between EV and internal-combustion propulsion too often.

Technical assistant Christi VanSyckle drove the Palisade Hybrid out to Colorado with her husband, daughter, and dogs in tow. “Even after a 15-hour driving day,” she wrote, “the comfort and ride were impressive the entire time.” However, her passengers also had challenges stowing the second-row captain’s chairs, choosing instead to just squeeze past them to access the third row. VanSyckle called out the Palisade’s steering during her road trip, appreciating its heft when the going got mountainous.

See all results for new 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid for sale near 28262.

Since the last patch, the Palisade took one trip to the dealer for its routine 16,000-mile service, which included an oil and filter change, a tire rotation, and the usual inspections. The cabin filter also should have been replaced, per the vehicle’s maintenance schedule, but for some reason, the dealer decided not to change that out. As is, the total for that visit came out to $164.

While we can certainly find tidbits that annoy us (we’re very good at that), our long-term Hyundai Palisade Hybrid doesn’t seem like it will be dethroned as the regent of road trips anytime soon. With 20,000 miles left, perhaps we’ll even be able to figure out how the second-row seats work.

In a recent development, going up north in Michigan often involves running the gamut of wild game crossing your path. With summer finally here, our trips up north have increased, as has our usage of the Hyundai Palisade Hybrid. Most of the fauna has been completely avoidable—with one exception.

Our 2026 Palisade Hybrid is equipped with factory built-in dash cams in the front and rear of the vehicle. They feature continuous-loop recording and parked motion/impact detection. The footage is stored to a MicroSD card. You can access the footage from the infotainment display and are able to look back at about two weeks' worth of clips (important to remember when you have this SUV in your possession).

Our most interesting recent clip came from managing testing editor David Beard, on his way up to Bear Lake, Michigan. A small bear crossed the Palisade Hybrid's path and didn't quite make it across before the right front corner of the SUV tagged it. Thanks to Beard's speedy reaction time, he slowed the SUV enough that it came away without any damage. As for the bear? At the time, we weren't quite sure. Would you check on a potentially very angry bear in the dead of night? A return trip the following day revealed that everyone appeared to make it out the unfortunate situation unscathed.

Sources indicate that beyond its ability to dodge live animals, the Palisade Hybrid has proven to be a great road-trip SUV. Many of our staffers cannot stop raving about the interior of this latest Palisade. Vehicle testing director Dave VanderWerp stated it's "comfortable, quiet, and seriously upscale." Buyer's Guide director (and current Genesis owner) Rich Ceppos thinks that "this is a full-fledged luxury car now, good enough to wear a Genesis badge. The ride is creamy, the powertrain smooth and quiet, the interior plush, and infotainment straightforward. It's a properly coddling driving experience." Sarah Taylor, online production assistant, agreed that the interior is comfortable and luxurious and further pointed to the Palisade's smooth ride. She also noted: "Slim A-pillars are much appreciated: no huge blind spots." Buyer's Guide managing editor Drew Dorian, who hauled some friends down to Cedar Point in Ohio, praised the seats. He said, "The adjustable side bolsters are a nice touch, and I even found our long-termer's kinetic seat feature useful after four days of riding rollercoasters.".

However, there have been a couple small gripes along the way. VanderWerp thought that the Palisade Hybrid "feels substantially larger and less wieldy than the previous model behind the wheel." And despite all the features it has, the Hyundai is missing one key capability: You cannot lock/unlock the rear doors with a touch of the door handle. That's "something every parent of small children would use daily," he said. As a mom of two handling no less than a purse, backpack, water bottle, and certainly a coffee mug at any given time, I fully agree.

At around 8400 miles, it was time for the Palisade Hybrid to head to the dealer for routine service. This visit included an oil change, tire rotation, and multipoint inspection for a total of $146. In addition, there was an open recall that needed to be addressed. Recall 297 pertains to the third-row seatbelt and wiring harness. If the third-row seatbelt is quickly pulled and creates sudden tension, the internal wiring harness could break or become unseated. Luckily, we had not experienced this problem. The dealer inspected the belt buckle and then installed a wiring harness extension to relieve the tension, which was all covered under warranty. Speaking of recalls and seats, our Palisade also got an over-the-air-upgrade fix for the unfortunate matter with the power second- and third-row seats that initially had inadequate pinch detection and caused a brief stop-sale for the new Palisade.

With another 30,000 miles to go, there's no telling where the Palisade Hybrid will take us next. Wherever it goes, we hope the on-board cameras don't pick up any more encounters with bears—or other wildlife.

Months in Fleet: 5 months Current Mileage: 11,265 milesAverage Fuel Economy: 25 mpg Fuel Tank Size: 18.2 gal Observed Fuel Range: 450 milesService: $146 Normal Wear: $0 Repair: $0Damage and Destruction: $0.

Hybrids continue popping up in greater numbers across the three-row SUV segment, and one such flower has grown tall enough to catch our eye rather quickly. After Hyundai introduced the redesigned Palisade for 2026, we snagged the upcoming hybrid variant for our annual 10Best competition, where it became an instant favorite. We decided to bring in the new award winner for an in-depth 40,000-mile evaluation.

We ended up with the top-trim Palisade Hybrid Calligraphy model, which starts at a modest $60,380, including the $2000 upcharge for all-wheel drive. Under the hood lies a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-four and two electric motors nestled within the standard six-speed automatic transmission. Since the Calligraphy is the Palisade's poshest trim, its list of standard equipment is pretty long, including all manner of active safety equipment, rain-sensing wipers, nappa-leather seats with massage for the driver, a tow hitch, a digital rearview mirror, power-adjustable second-row seats, and a head-up display. The only added option on the car was a $245 set of carpeted floor mats, bringing our Palisade Hybrid's total to $60,625.

Our initial testing brought in some respectable numbers for this large hybrid, which produces 329 horsepower and 339 pound-feet of torque. The SUV hustled to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds. Top-gear passing from 50 to 70 mph took place in a tidy 4.4 seconds, and the Palisade sprinted through the quarter-mile in 15.0 seconds at 94 mph. It managed 0.84 g of lateral grip around the skidpad (more than most families will need) and required just 170 feet to stop from 70 mph.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, it didn't take long for our latest long-termer to hit a snag. Upon receiving our upcoming Palisade Hybrid, we began our normal long-term onboarding process, which consists of removing the wheels and measuring the thickness of the brake pads. When we went to remove the pads, we found a wheel stud that was already stripped and spinning in place. The Palisade was promptly whisked away to the dealer and then disappeared for two months. Upon its return, we learned the dealer had to drill out the wheel stud and replace the damaged wheel hub. Ouch.

From there, it took only two weeks before another problem popped up: The engine started overheating. As soon as the car reached higher speeds—especially on the highway—the dashboard would launch into a series of chimes and warnings alerting us that the engine temperature was nearing the danger zone. The Hyundai went back to the dealer, who informed us that the water-pump belt had shredded itself alive. A fresh belt was installed, attachment points were tightened down, and we were assured it shouldn't happen again.

Sources indicate that the dealer also took care of a few recalls and service bulletins that had cropped up. The service department replaced front-bumper wiring related to the active front air flaps and installed two software updates, one of which was required to prevent potential instrument-cluster failure. All repairs and recalls were done under warranty at no cost.

It has been revealed that since the Palisade Hybrid returned for a second time, we've had no further issues. It went on a spring-break road trip to South Carolina and got back with no problems. We are hoping for more of the same as we rack up the miles on this well-dressed family hauler.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come.
  • Recent findings suggest that dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was unveiled without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams.
  • The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Recent findings suggest that dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was unveiled without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

In a recent development, the first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

In a recent development, the winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

It has been revealed that those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Recent findings suggest that not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

Industry observers note that PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G.

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be announced later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

  • Sources indicate that the first fresh arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of fresh content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

Sources indicate that the first fresh arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

It has been revealed that the Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Sources indicate that speaking of elemental reactions, upcoming in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

According to recent reports, then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

Recent findings suggest that the first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a upcoming outfit in the shop at a discount.

Recent findings suggest that version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside newly introduced stories of the Adepti.

Industry observers note that all around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

  • Procurement is now underway for zero-emission vehicles, equipment, and supporting infrastructure at four sites across the state.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Illinois Clean Ports Program is putting $104 million behind efforts to help clean up its working waterfronts, funds earmarked for heavy-duty electric equipment assets that includes forklifts, giant reach stackers, switcher locomotives, and the charging equipment needed to support them. There’s even a passenger ferry!

Procurement is now underway for zero-emission vehicles, equipment, and supporting infrastructure at four sites across the state. Administered by the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA), Illinois’ Clean Ports Program aims to modernize operations at ports and waterfront facilities in Chicago, the Quad Cities, and southern Illinois’ river port districts.

According to recent reports, “Illinois’ waterways are a competitive advantage for the state,” noted Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, who was elected to a historic third term on 03NOV. “By modernizing port infrastructure, advancing zero-emission technology, and improving air quality, we are strengthening our economy while building a cleaner future for Illinois.”.

Illinois’ Clean Ports Program isn’t just replacing diesel-powered equipment with electric alternatives – instead, the blueprint also includes Level 2 and DC fast charging, shore power and charging for electrified ships, and comprehensive grid upgrades designed to modernize existing port operations and support the deployment of new electric equipment.

In a recent development, the program takes a holistic approach to port electrification at Chicago’s Illinois International Port District (IIPD), treating energy generation, storage, and deployment as parts of a single connected system. On-site solar helps meet the port’s growing electricity needs while excess power is stored for peak hours, when grid electricity is most expensive. This setup reduces strain on the local grid, and acts as a hedge against rising energy costs.

It has been revealed that for smaller public port districts, replacing aging equipment and upgrading electrical infrastructure can be an enormous financial undertaking. The Illinois Clean Ports Program helps make those investments possible, bringing cleaner, healthier, zero-emission technology within reach of terminal operators while preparing the state’s ports for a more competitive freight future.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto.
  • Industry observers note that the feature is called Tesla Reality View, and it’s reaching early-access users with FSD V15.
  • Tesla’s biggest FSD V15 claim takes a little unpacking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tesla’s latest version of Full Self-Driving lets you swing a virtual camera around your car like you’re cruising through Leonida in Grand Theft Auto. It’s a neat trick, especially when you consider that the Tesla has to generate the scenery as it goes. It also gets a little floating arrow, which now lets you know which roundabout exit it’s going to take.

Industry observers note that the feature is called Tesla Reality View, and it’s reaching early-access users with FSD V15. The earlier parking display drew outlines of nearby objects, but this one recreates the street around you in real time and indicates where FSD intends to turn or park. You can have this on the whole screen, split it with the map, or let the map take over instead. There’s also a quieter cabin mode, and even the turn signal now fades sound after a few clicks.

Tesla’s biggest FSD V15 claim takes a little unpacking. The manufacturer claims it's now 25 times safer when it does critical interventions. The upgrade to the software that interprets camera images was trained on millions of internet videos and shared with its Robotaxi and Optimus programs.

What’s not clear is the starting figure. How many miles did the previous version go between critical interventions, and under what conditions? Tesla doesn’t say.

Will drivers actually notice? Tesla claims V15 is better at spotting potholes, small animals, signs, and debris, including chains (which have been known to cause crashes drawing federal scrutiny). It should also avoid deep standing water and choose more appropriate speeds in school zones and bad weather.

Tesla indicates the navigation now learns from the routes other Teslas actually take, initially at the start and end of a trip. Tesla prepares to extend that approach to the whole route later. Once you arrive, the map can show several parking options, and FSD uses your parking history to help pick one. It’s another application of the fleet learning feature Tesla demonstrated with V12.

Industry observers note that V15 can also slow for a speed camera, but if you override it twice for the same camera, the car will remember your preference. Bike Rack Mode lets FSD operate with a rack on the tow hitch, though it won’t automatically reverse for you at the destination, leaving parking up to you. Autopark, Summon and backup warnings are disabled in that mode.

Sources indicate that in a roughly 25-minute drive, Sawyer Merritt found V15 more cautious around pedestrians than V14. In one parking lot, he remarked the car braked for someone running across its path before he spotted them himself.

While parking, Merritt could see which space FSD had picked, but tapping another space did nothing. He had to switch to manual, select the spot, and reengage FSD. It then parked where he wanted. That parking maneuver makes a pretty good case for the GTA graphics, which now give you a much better idea of what’s around the car and what it’s about to do, but the 25-fold safety improvement claim will need more than a drive to Best Buy to judge.

GTA 6: Best Starter Car to Register

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, during your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car.
  • It has been revealed that this opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars.
  • It has been revealed that instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, during your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car. Registering cars allows you to call them easily from your phone with a small BuckMe fee.

It has been revealed that this opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars. To unlock Moses and his shop for good, you need to bring him your very first car to register.

It has been revealed that instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route. Here’s the best starter car to register in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that during the first mission of Chapter 2 in GTA 6, you will naturally meet a girl named Vicki. During this mission, Vicki will eventually mention Moses to Lucia, and once she does, Moses shop will be marked on the map with the objective to bring him a starter car to register.

After bringing Moses one car and registering it with him for free, you will unlock the ability to register most cars in Leonida. The only cars you can’t register with Moses are the ones with trackers, so make a mental note of that.

In a recent development, also, keep in mind that even though you can register your starter car for free, registering every other car from here on out will cost you money. The price of registration depends on the type of car.

According to recent reports, while players may want to steal and register the flashiest car in Leonida as their starter, this isn’t necessarily the smartest move. The nice sports cars won’t have the most trunk space and can be hard to control.

Instead, it would be best to choose a pickup truck for a starter car, as they have a ton of stash space and are generally easy to drive.

It may seem unimportant, but having more stash space will allow Lucia to transport more money and robbery loot on a single trip. This means you can gather money faster, without constantly needing to visit ATMs.

In a recent development, additionally, as previously mentioned, pickup trucks are generally on the easier side to control when driving. This is crucial early in the game since it will allow you to have an easier time exploring, crashing less, and avoiding the need to pay for repairs.

Once you've built up wealth by using your starter car as a getaway and stash for loot from robberies and muggings, you can use any extra cash to register nicer vehicles.

Simply put, the coolest cars tend to have the highest registration price, so you want a reliable one that will help you get around easier and stash more money to start off.

Recent findings suggest that while there are many pickup trucks to find across the map of GTA VI, I have had the best luck finding them in parking lots. More specifically, I have found pickup trucks commonly in parking lots in front of bars, clothing shops, barbershops, etc.

In other words, pickup trucks are very easy to find, considering they aren’t that special when it comes to style and speed and aren’t considered “rare.” If you are worried about finding one in a specific color, you shouldn’t be, considering Moses makes you change the color when you bring it in.

Once you find a pickup truck (or a different car if you decided not to listen to my advice), bring it on over to Moses and tell him you’d like to register it.

After the quick transaction with Moses is complete, you are now able to call your starter car to your location whenever you like for a small BuckMe price via the Scooter Bros app on your phone.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for decades, Briggs & Stratton has helped keep the lights on after the storm with its gas-powered generators.
  • Briggs & Stratton partnered with Texas-based EG4 to offer an all American-branded solution for battery backup power solution last year, and its stackable SimpliPHI batteries helped make it easy to right-size home battery projects – but those batteries were limited in size, and limited in what they could actually offer.
  • For context, the average US home uses about 865 kWh of energy per month, so a 512 kWh battery should theoretically keep your lights on for nearly 18 days after a storm – or provide basic power for your whole block for a weekend, at least!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for decades, Briggs & Stratton has helped keep the lights on after the storm with its gas-powered generators. Now, the company is bringing that legacy to the electric age with a upcoming 16 kWh backup battery designed to scale with your growing energy needs.

Briggs & Stratton partnered with Texas-based EG4 to offer an all American-branded solution for battery backup power solution last year, and its stackable SimpliPHI batteries helped make it easy to right-size home battery projects – but those batteries were limited in size, and limited in what they could actually offer. With the launch of the brand’s new, 16 kWh SimpliPHI battery, the firm is ready to meet your energy needs … even if those needs take you up to 512 kWh. (!).

For context, the average US home uses about 865 kWh of energy per month, so a 512 kWh battery should theoretically keep your lights on for nearly 18 days after a storm – or provide basic power for your whole block for a weekend, at least!

“This launch represents a significant shift in our battery strategy,” explains Sequoya Cross, vice president of energy storage at Briggs & Stratton. “Our combined resources allow us to bring a competitively priced battery of the highest quality to energy storage installers.”.

An onboard battery management system (BMS) and built-in Wi-Fi gateway help to streamline the system’s setup for installers, while the Briggs battery’s automatic inverter sensing technology supports closed-loop communication with Sol-Ark, Solis, EG4, Growatt, Megarevo, Victron, and other leading inverters. Other installer-friendly features include an IP65-rated enclosure allows for indoor or outdoor installation in either ground- or wall-mounted setups without requiring an additional cabinet, and an integrated circuit breaker that allows technicians to isolate the battery during servicing.

The battery itself is rated for 8,000 cycles at 90% depth of discharge, with a charge and discharge rate of 0.5C and an end-of-life capacity of 70%. Briggs & Stratton backs its newly introduced battery packs with a 12-year parts warranty that includes labor and travel costs, as well as a US-based tech support service.

The SimpliPHI 16 is available for pre-order now, though pricing was not mentioned in the original press release.

Heartopia, the upcoming cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a significant launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games declared today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find upcoming outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games indicates you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing upcoming inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Sources indicate that whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a significant game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

The U.S. Let Volvo Keep Selling Cars. Polestar Got A No. What About Mercedes?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Volvo EX-90 and Polestar 3 roll off the same assembly line in South Carolina.
  • Industry observers note that now Congress is considering a tougher law aimed at keeping Chinese cars out of the U.S., one that could reintroduce headaches for Volvo and put another major automaker in a tough position.
  • But the publication reported that Republican and Democratic lawmakers are nearing a deal that could spare Mercedes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Volvo EX-90 and Polestar 3 roll off the same assembly line in South Carolina. They share much of their hardware and, according to Polestar, run the same software. However, when each manufacturer asked Washington for permission to keep selling them in America, they got different answers.

Industry observers note that now Congress is considering a tougher law aimed at keeping Chinese cars out of the U.S., one that could reintroduce headaches for Volvo and put another major automaker in a tough position. Congress is close to a deal on legislation that would ban cars from automakers with more than 15% Chinese ownership stake, as Bloomberg reported. This would be a tough pill for Mercedes-Benz, as around 20% of the organization's stock is owned by Chinese investors.

But the publication reported that Republican and Democratic lawmakers are nearing a deal that could spare Mercedes. They want to send a bill to the president by the end of the year, but its terms have not yet been finalized.

Volvo EX90 assembly at the Volvo Ridgeville factory in South Carolina.

In a recent development, the Volvo and Polestar decisions came under a Commerce Department rule finalized in 2025 aimed at controlling connectivity and self-driving technology. Washington’s concern is that a foreign adversary could use those systems to collect data on Americans or even remotely control vehicles. The new restrictions on certain Chinese- or Russian-linked software take effect for the 2027 model year. Hardware restrictions will follow in 2030 and apply to both gas and electric cars, including ones assembled on U.S. soil.

Chinese giant Geely has a majority stake in Volvo Cars, so the Swedish automaker had to apply for specific authorization to keep importing and selling connected cars. The Department of Commerce granted it. Volvo told InsideEVs it still has to meet the same software requirements as every other automaker. The Swedish foreign trade minister confirmed his government worked closely with Volvo to achieve compliance.

In a recent development, polestar is another Sweden-based automaker that is controlled by Geely. It applied and was denied authorization to keep selling cars from model year 2027 onward. So why was Polestar axed despite Volvo being saved? Polestar told its dealers it had asked the Department of Commerce that very question and had yet to get an explanation, pointing to the common software and the shared South Carolina production line.

Sources indicate that even though Polestar is a Volvo spinoff and also has a Swedish connection, the country’s trade minister remarked Polestar didn’t want the same assistance as Volvo. That’s one difference we know between their applications, but the U.S. government hasn’t explicitly said why things shook out this way, and Polestar did not appeal the decision.

Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV production in Alabama.

Industry observers note that the proposed Connected Vehicle Security Act would write existing restrictions into federal law and extend the U.S. sales ban to automakers with more than 15% Chinese ownership, even if they build their cars in America.

China’s state-owned BAIC Group owns 9.98% of Mercedes-Benz. Geely founder Li Shufu holds another 9.69% through an investment company. Taken together, that’s just shy of 20%, and over the new proposed threshold.

For reference, Geely owns 79% of Volvo and Geely founder Li Shufu reported beneficial ownership of 60.5% of Polestar’s shares in a September 2026 SEC filing.

That doesn't mean Mercedes will be locked out of the market, though, even if the bill passes as currently written.

Industry observers note that “The U.S. is an extremely key market for us, and we're not going to do anything to jeopardize our success in the past and our success in the future,” Jason Hoff, CEO of Mercedes-Benz North America, said during a media roundtable with InsideEVs last week.

When asked whether the tech giant had a blueprint for its Chinese shareholders to divest, Hoff declined to comment on specific conversations Mercedes has with shareholders. He was more direct about the legislation itself.

In a recent development, “You know, we always have and always will support anything that protects the national security of the United States. So we've never opposed this bill, but you know, in the end, we'll also take whatever steps we need to comply with it if it does get passed," Hoff said.

Mercedes claims its Chinese shareholders have no seats on its management board and no say in day-to-day decisions. They could still have voting rights as shareholders. That matters because, according to Bloomberg, lawmakers are considering an exception that would let companies exclude passive investments with no voting rights from the proposed 15% ownership calculation.

Recent findings suggest that it’s still unclear how Mercedes would prove its Chinese stakes qualify. In the meantime, House members have asked Mercedes to provide documents, answer two dozen questions by December 1, and arrange a meeting with its U.S. boss.
